- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes or high values.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true values by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct quickly, leading to overprediction in subsequent days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates when prices are high and underestimates when prices are low, but fails to adjust smoothly.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizons show persistent underestimation of downward trends and overestimation of upward trends, especially in the first 10–15 days.
- Model is overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to exaggerated forecasts when history includes recent peaks.
- When true values are trending downward, model often fails to recognize the slope, continuing to predict higher values for several days.
- Model underestimates volatility in early periods, leading to overly conservative forecasts when actual price swings are larger than expected.
